Es gibt keine D/L-Beschriftung, keine Keilbindungen, keine bezeichnete Fischerprojektion und keine Behauptung, Glycin sei chiral.

originalRecord.desktop680Finding: Bei636px sind Gruppen, vier Bindungsarme und Ladungszeichen gut erkennbar. Keine abgeschnittenen Gruppen oder verdeckten Zeichen.

nativeConcreteFindings: Oben zeigt dasselbe verbundene blaue/rosa Lactosemodell eine passende grüne Enzymtasche; danach liegen genau zwei getrennte Bausteine vor. wholeCurrentGoalWithCandidateLink.description: Die lernende Person kann für vorgegebene Waschbedingungen und Zielkriterien ausgewählte Tensidstrukturen anhand ihrer Struktur-Eigenschafts-Beziehungen vergleichen und eine begründete Strukturwahl zur Verbesserung einer Waschmittelformulierung treffen.
wholeCurrentGoalWithCandidateLink.descriptionEn: The learner can compare selected surfactant structures using structure-property relationships for specified washing conditions and objectives,and make a justified structure choice to improve a detergent formulation.

resourceLinks.title: Visualisierung: Tensidstrukturen optimieren
resourceLinks.description: Schematischer Strukturvergleich: Kopfgruppe passend zu Waschbedingungen und getrennten Zielkriterien auswählen; keine allgemeine Rangfolge.
resourceLinks.altText: Zwei schematische Tensidbauformen stehen gleichwertig nebeneinander: Beide haben einen orangefarbenen unpolaren Schwanz und einen blauen hydrophilen Bereich. Links besitzt der Kopf eine negative Ladung; rechts ist der ungeladene hydrophile Bereich verlängert. Darüber stehen Temperatur, Wasserhärte und Dosis als Waschbedingungen. Ein fettbeflecktes Tuch und Schaumblasen stehen für getrennte Zielkriterien. Die offene Frage „Welche Struktur passt?“ lässt die begründete Auswahl offen.

independence.basis: Read the full current German/English goal, candidate link and ALT, both complete selected P cases/rubrics, the actual original generation prompt and actual edit prompt. Viewed the native exact PNG and both fresh own actual unchanged React GoalCard screenshots with view_image. The author is not treated as an independent V reviewer.

nativeConcreteFindings: The two pale comparison panels contain no A/B letters or replacement case identifiers. No candidate letter is attached to the charged or uncharged head.

Both symbolic structures have an orange unpolar tail connected to a blue hydrophilic region. The left compact head has a clear minus sign; the right extended three-lobe hydrophilic region has no charge sign. The lobes are a schematic segment, without an atom-by-atom formula claim.
Small water droplets appear beside both blue head regions, not beside the orange tails. This supports the hydrophilic/unpolar contrast without portraying a quantitative hydration measurement.
The top row names Temperatur, Wasserhärte and Dosis. It supplies no numerical thresholds and does not state that increasing any variable improves every formulation.

The bottom cloth/oil stain and foam are separate objective motifs. The open question Welche Struktur passt? is placed between them. There are no ticks, ranking arrows, performance bars, greater-is-better foam comparisons, selected winners or environmental approval claims.

wholeCaseConsistency.finding: The complete case table assigns A to C12 sulfate, B to a linear sulfonate and C to C12 ethoxylate. The final image has no letter-to-structure assignments, so its neutral hydrophilic segment does not conflict with table B being anionic. The picture supplies none of the dose, Krafft or cloud-point values and does not select C. The 45°C transfer still requires fresh reasoning and further data.

The D/E comparison and untested F/G mixture require independent use of temperature, head hydration, fat-removal data and foam constraints. The image does not assign these letters, assert a mixture compatibility result or equate foam with fat removal. Its two equally prominent structures preserve the open choice required by the case.

originalRecord.altAndGoalFit: The complete current ALT accurately describes orange tails, blue hydrophilic regions, one negative head, one extended uncharged segment, three conditions, two separate objectives and an unanswered choice. The picture supports conditional structure selection in the current AB3 goal; it does not claim an actual optimization experiment, a synthesis or a universal winner.
originalRecord.mobile360Finding: At 360px card width the actual image is approximately 316×177.84px. The minus sign, both connected tails, distinct head regions, three condition icons/labels, cloth and foam motifs, and central open question remain distinguishable. All content is contained; no cropped head, text or tail was observed.
originalRecord.desktop680Finding: At 680px card width the actual image is approximately 636×357.94px. The same chemical distinctions and labels are clear and fully visible. The 448px image-height limit is not reached.
originalRecord.formatDecision: KEEP the existing 1672×941 landscape PNG (approximately 16:9). Two side-by-side symbolic structures and short labels remain usable in both measured GoalCards. No aspect-ratio, provider or file-format replacement is scientifically justified by this inspection.

provenance.boundary: Source generation and the targeted edit are recorded from their stored prompts. The model version was not exposed. Prompt intent, author assertions, previous rejection and historical human/AI flags do not constitute this V decision. No claim is made that every pixel outside the removed letters is byte-identical to the previous PNG.

scientificAndScopeLimits: The molecular icons are not exact sulfate, sulfonate or EO6 formulas and do not encode carbon count or a calibrated chain-length difference.
The water-hardness icon is qualitative. The image proves neither universal hardness tolerance nor a universal cloud/Krafft threshold. Such judgments require the case data.
The positions of cloth and foam identify objectives; no arrow or label assigns oil removal exclusively to the left class or foam exclusively to the right class.
An orientation image does not prove learner performance, actual formulation testing, P/D/A/M coverage, source coverage or host/workflow acceptance.
